chunks: Ghayba of al-Tusi: A group informed us, from Abi Muhammad al-Tali'ukbari, from Abi Ali Muhammad ibn Hammam who said:

Al-Shari'i was known as Abi Muhammad. Harun said: I think his name was al-Hasan. He was among the companions of Abi al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), and then al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) after him. He was the first to claim a station that Allah did not assign to him, and for which he was not worthy. He lied about Allah and His Proofs (peace be upon them), and attributed to them that which is not fitting for them, and they are free from it. The Shia cursed him and disassociated from him. A Tawqi (decree) of the Imam (peace be upon him) came out cursing him and disassociating from him. Harun said: Then he manifested the statement of disbelief and heresy.

key_terms.تَوْقِيعٌ: Tawqi (decree or letter from the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Who was al-Shari'i and why was he cursed by the Shia?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Tusi's *Ghayba* identifies al-Shari'i as a pivotal figure in the early Shia schism, specifically during the Minor Exile, where he was the first to claim a unique, divinely-ordained station (*maqam*) for himself, leading to his excommunication (*tawqi'*). His transition from a companion of the Imams to a proponent of heresy (*ilhad*) illustrates the critical process of distinguishing authentic Imamate authority from false claims during the period of occultation. This event underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on verifying the credentials of those who claim proximity to the Imams to prevent doctrinal deviation.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/257] Ghayba of al-Tusi: A large number from Abi Muhammad [Harun] al-Tali’ukbari from Abi Ali Muhammad b. Hammam who said:

al-Shari’i had the Kuniyya Abi Muhammad [Harun said: I think his name was al-Hasan] and he was one of the companions of Abi al-Hasan Ali b. Muhammad [al-Naqi] عليه السلام and then al-Hasan b. Ali [al-Askari] عليه السلام after him. He was the first to claim a station that Allah did not bestow on him and for which he was not suited. He lied upon Allah and His Proofs عليهم السلام and attributed to them that which is not fitting to them and which they are disassociated from. Then the Shia cursed him and disassociated from him. A Tawqi of the Imam عليه السلام came out in cursing and disassociating from him. Harun said: He [Shari’i] ultimately manifested a call to outright disbelief and heresy.
